source.title: On three open problems related to quasi relative interior

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separated locally convex topological vector space. For a subset S of X, let cone(S) denote the conic hull of S and let cl(cone(S)) denote its closure in X. For a convex set E in X, define the quasi-relative interior qri(E) as the set of points x in E such that cl(cone(E - x)) is a linear subspace of X. For convex sets C and D in X, define the Minkowski sum C + D as {c + d : c in C and d in D}. Since qri(C) + qri(D) is always contained in qri(C + D), can this inclusion be proper? Equivalently, do there exist convex sets C and D in a separated locally convex space X such that qri(C) + qri(D) is a proper subset of qri(C + D)?

evidence.quote: Throughout the paper, if not specified otherwise, X is a separated locally convex space and X ∗ is its topological dual.
For A, B ⊂ X, a ∈ X, Γ ⊂ R and γ ∈ R we set A + B := {a + b | a ∈ A, b ∈ B}, a + A := {a} + A,

Let C ⊂ X be a convex set; the quasi interior of C (see [1, p. 2544]) is the set qi C := {x ∈ C | cone(C − x) = X} , and the quasi relative interior of C (see [2, Def. 2.3]) is the set qri C := {x ∈ C | cone(C − x) is a linear space} ;
qri C + qri D = qri(qri C + qri D) ⊂ qri(C + D)
Borwein and Goebel, in [1, p. 2548], say “Can qri C+qri D be a proper subset of qri(C+D)? (Almost certainly such sets do exist.)”
The next example answers to both problems mentioned above.

For a convex set E in X, define the quasi interior qi(E) as the set of points x in E such that cl(cone(E - x)) equals X. For convex sets A and B in X, define A + B as {a + b : a in A and b in B}. If qi(B) is nonempty, must the equality A + qi(B) = qi(A + B) always hold?

Grad and Pop, in [5, p. 26], say: “we conjecture that in general when A, B ⊆ V are convex sets with qi B 6= ∅, it holds A + qi B = qi(A + B)”.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separated locally convex topological vector space. For a subset S of X, let cone(S) denote the conic hull of S and let cl(cone(S)) denote its closure in X. For a nonempty convex set E in X, define the quasi-relative interior qri(E) as the set of points x in E such that cl(cone(E - x)) is a linear subspace of X. Let C and D be nonempty convex subsets of X with qri(C) intersect qri(D) nonempty. Must qri(C intersect D) be contained in qri(C) intersect qri(D), or can this inclusion fail?

evidence.quote: Throughout the paper, if not specified otherwise, X is a separated locally convex space and X ∗ is its topological dual.

Let C ⊂ X be a convex set; the quasi interior of C (see [1, p. 2544]) is the set qi C := {x ∈ C | cone(C − x) = X} , and the quasi relative interior of C (see [2, Def. 2.3]) is the set qri C := {x ∈ C | cone(C − x) is a linear space} ;
Proposition 3 Let C, D ⊂ X be nonempty convex sets.
(ii) If qri C ∩ qri D 6= ∅ then qri(C ∩ D) ⊂ qri C ∩ qri D.
Borwein and Goebel, in [1, p. 2548], also say “Can qri(C ∩ D) ⊂ qri C ∩ qri D fail when qri C ∩ qri D 6= ∅? ”
Proposition 3 (ii) shows that the answer to this question is negative.
